title: PARSRec: Explainable Personalized Attention-fused Recurrent Sequential Recommendation Using Session Partial Actions

problem.claim: Recommender systems must help users navigate very large online-market search spaces by offering items of interest.

gap.claim: Systems that learn common user behaviors can overlook subtle individual differences between users.

contributions.claim: An architecture is proposed that combines common patterns with individual behaviors to personalize recommendations.
In a controlled simulation environment, the proposed model learns interpretable personalized user behaviors.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Controlled-environment simulations show that the proposed model learns interpretable personalized user behaviors.
Experiments on the Nielsen Consumer Panel dataset report up to 27.9% performance improvement over the state-of-the-art.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online markets create large product search spaces where recommender systems help users find items of interest.
Learning common user behaviors is effective but can miss individual idiosyncrasies.
The authors propose combining common patterns and individual behaviors to tailor recommendations.
Controlled simulations report interpretable personalized behaviors, and Nielsen Consumer Panel experiments report up to 27.9% improvement over the state-of-the-art.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the architecture, attention mechanism, recurrent formulation, or use of session partial actions.
The abstract does not provide evaluation metrics, experimental settings, baselines, or statistical uncertainty for the reported 27.9% improvement.
